This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
This is an application for bail.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

The appellant-petitioner has been convicted under section 376(1)/323 of the I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo R.I. for a period of twelve years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- (rupees ten thousand), in default, to undergo R.I. for a further period of one year for the offence under section 376(1) of the I.P.C. and to undergo S.I. for one month for the offence under section 323 of the I.P.C. and both the sentences were directed // 2 // to run concurrently by the learned Sessions Judge, Angul in C.T.(S)
Case No.09 of 2018.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner was taken into judicial custody since 11.09.2017 and he was never released on bail by the learned trial Court or by this Court during pendency of this appeal and out of twelve years of substantive sentence imposed by the learned trial Court, the petitioner has already undergone half of the sentence and there is no chance of early Anil Nath vs State Of Odisha on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120989920/
1 hearing of the appeal in the near future and therefore, the petitioner may be granted interim bail for some period.
Learned counsel for the State submitted that earlier the bail application of the petitioner was rejected on merit as per order dated 02.09.2021 in I.A. No.2033 of 2019.

entities.text: Anil Nath vs State Of Odisha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties

, since the petitioner has undergone half of the substantive sentence and there is no chance of early hearing of the appeal in the near future, I am inclined to release him on interim bail for a period of three months from the date of release.
The petitioner shall immediately surrender before the learned Court below on expiry of the said three months period.

For the above period, let the petitioner be released on interim bail to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court in connection with the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/-(rupees fifty thousand) with two // 3 // local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin over the matter including the conditions that the petitioner shall not indulge in any criminal activities.
Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
The I.A. is disposed of accordingly.
Issue urgent certified copy as per Rules.
( S.K. Sahoo) Judge 09.
List this matter in the week commencing from 29th January 2024.
Learned counsel for the appellant shall file the surrender certificate of the appellant in the meantime.
